question: Will Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian personally deliver Iran's statement at the UNGA 81 general debate (22–28 September 2026)?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: Pezeshkian is on the UN provisional speaker list for the 23 Sept morning session as 'President Masoud Pezeshkian', visas for the core delegation (him + Araghchi) were granted 17 Sept, Araghchi's advance party left Tehran 20 Sept, and IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV confirm a 22 Sept departure. Reference class: Iran's president has been the speaker of record for Iran's national statement in every general debate for the last ~12 sessions (12/12, including video-message years 2020-21, which the fine print counts as YES); Laplace ~93%. Conditioning on visa granted + slot listed + delegation already in transit + slot falling on day 2 of the window pushes above that; the pre-recorded-video escape hatch also converts most travel-failure scenarios into YES. Counterargument: seventh month of an active US/Israel-Iran war, Trump publicly weighing resumed large-scale strikes, hardline domestic pressure on the trip, a US administration that has revoked/denied Iranian visas elsewhere in 2026 (already denied his media team) - any of which could force a recall and hand the statement to Araghchi, who is already in New York and is the natural substitute. Those tails justify ~5%, not more, with only ~1.6 days between Now and the slot. No prediction market prices this contract (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi checked, none found), so no crowd anchor.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the finalized UN General Debate portal record (gadebate.un.org) speaker list / video archive for 'Iran (Islamic Republic of)', read 1-2 Oct 2026 - NOT off live coverage, NOT off announced schedules. A pre-recorded video message counts the same as in-person, so long as Pezeshkian is the speaker of record. Any other speaker (FM, PR, delegate) or no statement = NO. A slot slipping to 29 Sept+ still counts.

EVENT WINDOW: 22-28 September 2026 (general debate: 22-26 and 28 Sept) per the criteria; as of Now 2026-09-21T18:44Z, 0% elapsed - the debate has not begun. Iran's published slot is the morning of 23 Sept, i.e. ~1.6 days after Now.

EVIDENCE (both directions):
- The published UNGA 81 general-debate lineup lists Iran in the 23 Sept MORNING session as 'President Masoud Pezeshkian' (Wikipedia mirror of the UN provisional list of speakers, accessed 21 Sept 2026). UN speaker lists are provisional and the LEVEL (head of state vs FM) can be revised in the daily Journal.
- US State Dept granted visas on 17 Sept 2026 to a 'core' Iranian delegation explicitly covering Pezeshkian and FM Abbas Araghchi, framed as a host-country obligation; delegation smaller than 2025, with travel-radius and purchasing restrictions (NBC News, Al Jazeera, 17 Sept 2026).
- IRNA reported 21 Sept that the US denied visas to other delegation members including the president's media/PR team, calling it 'unprecedented hostile action' (ANI, LatestLY, Press TV, 20-21 Sept 2026).
- Araghchi departed Tehran leading a diplomatic delegation on the evening of 20 Sept 2026, a day ahead of the president (Iranian state media via IranWire/Press TV). Araghchi is therefore already positioned in New York.
- Iranian state media (IRNA, Tasnim) say Pezeshkian departs Tehran 22 Sept and addresses the Assembly 23 Sept morning, plus sideline meetings with foreign leaders, Iranian expatriates and US think tanks (ANI / LatestLY / Press TV, 20-21 Sept 2026).
- WAR CONTEXT: the US-Israel-Iran war began February 2026 and is in its seventh month. Trump said 17 Sept he faces 'a big decision' on whether to resume large-scale attacks; Iran's military says it expects renewed US strikes and has vowed retaliation 'without limitations' (CNBC, Fox News, RFE/RL, 17-21 Sept 2026).
- COUNTER-SIGNAL TOWARD DIPLOMACY: Trump said 20 Sept he is open to meeting Pezeshkian; US UN Ambassador Waltz said Trump is 'always open to a deal'; markets rose on the Iranian delegation's UN attendance (CNBC, 21 Sept 2026).
- DOMESTIC FRICTION: Iranian hardline factions have attacked Pezeshkian through 2026 over defending negotiations with Washington; reformists frame the UN trip as dependent on a Khamenei mandate (Iran International, May-June 2026 and Sept coverage). Searched for any explicit 2026 hardline demand that he cancel the trip, or any Khamenei veto - none found.

BASE RATES:
- Over the last 12 UNGA general debates (sessions 69-80, 2014-2025), Iran's national statement was delivered by the sitting President in all 12: Rouhani 2014-2020 (2020 by pre-recorded video), Raisi 2021 (video)-2023, Pezeshkian 2024 and 2025. Source: UN general debate records / UN Web TV archives. Class = 'all sessions', unconditional on circumstances.
- Conditional sub-class 'Iran's president under acute US-Iran tension or visa friction' (2019 visa-delay standoff; 2022-2023 post-protest sessions): the president still delivered in each instance.
- Conditional sub-class 'travel physically impossible / pandemic': Iran still delivered a presidential statement, by pre-recorded video (2020, 2021) - i.e. the failure mode historically produced video, not substitution.
- 2025 precedent specifically: Pezeshkian travelled to New York 23 Sept 2025 and delivered Iran's statement 24 Sept 2025.
- Broader class 'head of state named on the UN provisional speaker list 1-2 days out, visas in hand, travel underway, who is nonetheless replaced by a minister': uncommon but non-zero; drivers are domestic crisis, health, or a security event. No published count of this rate was found.

MARKETS: harness title search found no candidate on Polymarket or Manifold. Own check of Kalshi's Iran category (21 Sept 2026) found only US-Iran nuclear-deal, Strait-of-Hormuz-closure and regime-recognition contracts - nothing on who delivers a UNGA statement. No bookmaker line found. Treat as: no market on this contract.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: the raw UN provisional/revised list of speakers PDF for the 81st session (gadebate.un.org returned no readable content to the fetch tool; the e-delegate speaker system was not accessible); any report of Pezeshkian's own visa being revoked or of the trip being cancelled; any statement that Araghchi would deliver the national statement; any 2026 report of Khamenei blocking the trip.

calls.reasoning: Iran's sitting president has been the speaker of record for Iran's general-debate statement every year for ~two decades (in person 2022-2025, by video in 2020-2021), so the class prior is ~0.93-0.95. Conditioning sharply raises it: as of 2026-09-21 the US has issued visas to Pezeshkian and Araghchi, FM Araghchi's delegation departed Tehran 20 Sept, IRNA published the itinerary (depart 22 Sept, address the GA 23 Sept morning), and Tehran publicly refused to downgrade over the denied media-team visas. US restrictions announced are on movement/purchases in NYC, not attendance. Main counterargument: an active seven-month US-Israel/Iran war makes a recall, security incident, or last-minute hand-off to Araghchi (already in New York) more plausible than in a normal year, and Washington has blocked Iranian officials' movements elsewhere in 2026 - but his slot falls on day 2 of a 22-28 Sept window (with post-28 Sept slots still counting YES), so exposure is ~36 hours. No prediction market on this event exists on Polymarket, Kalshi, or Manifold, so there is no crowd anchor; evidence is one-sided toward YES and largely sourced from Iranian state media relayed by wires, which I discount slightly.

EVIDENCE (both directions):
- IRNA via ANI/LatestLY, 21 Sep 2026: Pezeshkian scheduled to depart Tehran for New York Tue 22 Sep; address the GA Wed 23 Sep, morning session; sideline meetings with heads of state, Iranian expatriates, US think tanks.

Article states bilateral meetings planned 22-29 Sep; contains no indication of cancellation or downgrade.
- Channels TV / Reuters-style wire, 21 Sep 2026: Iranian state media call the media-team visa denials an 'unprecedented hostile action'; FM spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the US measures 'crude propaganda'; Iran proceeding regardless.
- Washington Post, 17 Sep 2026: US said it would permit a 'core' Iranian delegation covering the president; delegation smaller than 2025.
- Fox News, 21 Sep 2026: Pezeshkian would be the highest-ranking Iranian official to enter the US since the war began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February 2026; war is in its seventh month.
- Context risk: a head of state speaking in New York while his country is at war with the US is described in coverage as near-unprecedented; wartime conditions create recall/security/escalation risk during the trip. The US has restricted or blocked Iranian officials' movements in other 2026 instances.
- Counter-risk on the other side: Araghchi is already in New York and is the standing fallback speaker for Iran if the president does not appear.

BASE RATES:
- Over all UNGA general debates 2005-2025, Iran's statement was delivered by the sitting president: Ahmadinejad 2005-2013, Rouhani 2014-2020, Raisi 2021-2023, Pezeshkian 2024-2025. 2020 and 2021 were pre-recorded video messages by the president (COVID-era / Raisi's first session); 2022-2025 in person. Source: UN general-debate records and the Wikipedia general-debate session pages.
- Over the subclass 'sitting Iranian president with US entry visa granted and travel underway': 2024 and 2025 (Pezeshkian traveled to New York 23 Sep 2025 and delivered the statement 24 Sep 2025), 2022 and 2023 (Raisi), 2014-2019 (Rouhani) - no known instance in that conditional subclass of the statement being handed to the foreign minister after the president had departed.
- Over the broader class 'any head of state/government with a published UNGA itinerary and a scheduled slot <48h away': downgrades to FM/deputy do occur (domestic crisis, illness, schedule collision) but are uncommon; UNGA speaker lists are revised repeatedly during high-level week, so a listed head of state is not a guarantee.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: (a) the UN provisional list of speakers PDF / gadebate.un.org speaker entry for Iran - the portal returned no usable content on fetch, so the official listed level for Iran on 23 Sep could not be confirmed this run; (b) any prediction market on this event - no contract found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search) or via my own search; Kalshi and bookmakers surfaced nothing; (c) any report dated 21 Sep 2026 of the trip being cancelled, postponed, or the address reassigned; (d) confirmation that Pezeshkian's plane had actually departed Tehran (departure is prospective as of Now); (e) any Iranian domestic-political reporting on hardliner pressure to abandon the trip.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: Absent an intervening shock, the announced schedule executes and the sitting Iranian president is the speaker of record, as in every recent session.

BASE RATES:
- Over all Iranian national statements at the UNGA general debate, sessions 60-80 (2005-2025): the sitting president was the speaker of record in every session - Ahmadinejad 2005-2012, Rouhani 2013-2020, Raisi 2021-2023, Pezeshkian 2024 and 2025 (UN General Debate portal; gadebate.un.org/en/80/iran-islamic-republic; UN Web TV session archives for 76th, 78th, 79th). Two of those (75th in 2020, 76th in 2021) were pre-recorded video, which under these criteria is the same outcome. I found no session in that range where Iran's foreign minister or permanent representative delivered the general-debate statement; I searched specifically for such a case and could not find one, so treat this as ~21/21 with search-coverage uncertainty on the older years.
- Conditional on the president having a publicly announced travel date, an issued US visa, and a named debate slot roughly one day out: the general cross-country rate of such a leader personally delivering is on the order of 95-97%; I could not find a published dataset computing this, so it is constructed from the pattern of announced-then-delivered UNGA slots rather than a cited series.
- Conditional on Iran specifically: in 2025 (session 80) Pezeshkian traveled to New York on 23 Sep and delivered on 24 Sep under a comparable set of US-imposed restrictions and a tight security perimeter.
- Counter-direction precedent: Ahmadinejad cancelled a New York trip in March 2007, citing US visa handling, after it had been publicly announced (Al Jazeera, 23 Mar 2007). That was a Security Council session, not the general debate, but it is the one documented instance of an Iranian president scrapping an announced UN trip late.
- In 2024 (session 79), Pezeshkian delivered the statement but his scheduled New York press conference was cancelled the same day after domestic conservative backlash - evidence that domestic political pressure can cut ancillary events without cutting the address itself.

Conditioning moves it up, not down: US visas issued 17 Sept to Pezeshkian and Araghchi as a host-country obligation, FM Araghchi's delegation departed Tehran 20 Sept, the president's office (Habibollah Abbasi, via IRNA) published departure 22 Sept and a 23 Sept morning address, Tehran publicly refused to downgrade over the denied media-team visas, and US restrictions announced target movement radius and purchases in NYC rather than attendance. Only ~37 hours separate the anchor from the slot, and a slot slipping past 28 Sept still counts YES. Main counterargument: month seven of an active US-Israel-Iran war with Trump publicly weighing resumed strikes, Pezeshkian had not physically departed at the anchor time, and Araghchi is already in New York as a ready substitute if a recall occurs mid-trip (the 2007 Ahmadinejad cancellation of an announced UN trip is the one Iranian precedent, though for a Security Council session). calls.reconciliation: All three runs reached 0.950 from the same evidence, so there was no numerical dispute to arbitrate - the work was checking whether the reconciled evidence sits at that number. Factual disputes: (1) whether the UN provisional speaker list names Pezeshkian at head-of-state level for the 23 Sept morning slot - Run 1 asserts it via a Wikipedia mirror of the UN list, Runs 2 and 3 both report gadebate.un.org returned no retrievable content on fetch and explicitly could not confirm the listed level. No web access on this run, so this cannot be settled; I treat it as weak supporting evidence rather than confirmation, noting that the itinerary itself is independently attested by three separate wire chains carrying IRNA and by Mehr, Tehran Times and IranWire. (2) Araghchi's routing (Run 3: via Qatar; Runs 1-2: direct, a day ahead) - immaterial to resolution, and all three agree he is en route or arrived, which is what matters for the substitute-speaker branch. (3) Whether Pezeshkian had departed Tehran as of the anchor - all three converge on NOT YET departed, with Run 3 flagging that past-tense arrival snippets appear to conflate the 2025 session 80 visit; I adopt not-departed, which is the more conservative reading. Judgment disputes: Run 3 weighs Khamenei's rejection of direct US talks and IRGC Hormuz attacks as downward pressure; I discount this, because those bear on whether negotiations happen, not on whether the president reads a national statement - Iran's 2024 precedent (address delivered, ancillary press conference cancelled under conservative backlash) shows domestic pressure cutting side events rather than the address. Run 2's discount for Iranian-state-media sourcing is fair but the itinerary is corroborated by US-side visa reporting (Washington Post, NBC, Al Jazeera, 17 Sept), which is independent. I land at 0.96, marginally above all three: their 0.95 is essentially the unconditional class prior, but the conditioning set here - visas in hand, delegation in transit, named slot on day two of the window, a pre-recorded-video pathway that converts travel failure into YES, and slots after 28 Sept still counting - is strictly stronger than the unconditional case, and the 37-hour exposure window bounds the war-escalation tail. Market check: no contract found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search) and none on Kalshi or bookmakers in any of the three runs' independent checks; no crowd anchor, so nothing to blend.
